Learnedly from χρονο- (chrono-) + διάγραμμα (diágramma), a calque of English timetable.
Learnedly from χρονο- (chrono-) + διακόπτης (diakóptis), a calque of English time switch.
From Ancient Greek κτενίζω (ktenízō, “to comb”). By surface analysis, χτένα (chténa, “a comb”) + -ίζω (-ízo). The third sense, to "comb, search", is a semantic loan from English comb.
Learned borrowing from English hobby.
Calque of English baked Alaska.
By surface analysis, ψηφιακός (psifiakós, “digital”) + υπογραφή (ypografí, “signature”). Calque of English digital signature.
Calque of English digital. From ψηφί(ο) n (psifí(o), “digit”) + -ακός (-akós, suffix for adjectives). Also see Koine Greek ψηφίον (psēphíon).
ψηφίο (psifío, “digit”) + -ποίηση (-poíisi, “-ization”), calque of English digitization.
Learned borrowing from English psychosomatic. Morphologically, from ψυχο- (psycho-, “ψυχή soul”) + σωματικός (somatikós, “bodily, corporal”).
ωο- (oo-, “oo- (egg)”) + γένεση (génesi, “creation - birth”). Learned borrowing from English oogenesis.
From ωφέλιμος (ofélimos, “useful”) + -ισμός (-ismós, “-ism”), a calque of English utilitarianism.

Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ὕφος (húphos, “weaving, fabric”), from ὑφή (huphḗ, “web”) + -ος (-os, “action noun suffix”). For the "linguistic register" sense, semantic loan from English register; for the "expression" sense, semantic loan from French style.

Learnedly, from Ancient Greek ἐξερευνῶ (exereunô) < ἐξ (ex) + ἐρευνῶ (ereunô). A semantic loan from French explorer or from English explore. By surface analysis, εξ- (ex-, “from”) + ερευνώ (erevnó, “search, investigate”).

Perfect participle of καταψύχομαι (katapsýchomai), passive voice of καταψύχω (katapsýcho). Semantic loan from French surgelé or from English refrigerated. The medieval κατεψυγμένος (katepsugménos), with different sense: "destroyed from cold".

Either inherited from Byzantine Greek or learned borrowing from Koine Greek πείραμα (peírama, “result of experience”), from Ancient Greek πειρῶμαι (peirômai) + -μα (-ma) (see Ancient Greek πειρᾰ́ω (peirắō)), with semantic loan from English experiment.

parole.significato: class (military; persons subject to the same intake)
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek σειρά (seirá). The sense “TV series” is a semantic loan from French série or from English serial.

Learnedly, from Ancient Greek χάρτης (“a papyrus scroll”), semantic loan from Italian carta or from English chart, from Latin charta, from Ancient Greek χάρτης (khártēs). Doublet of κάρτα (kárta, “card”).

Unadapted learned borrowing either from English Hindi, Hindi हिंदी (hindī) or Classical Persian هندی (hindī). As neuter plural with article τα (ta), in the pattern of substantivised adjectives for language names; compare αγγλικά n pl (angliká, “English”). As feminine with article η (i), by ellipsis
